method_fomc: The range is what the Federal Open Market Committee sets at each meeting. A new range takes effect the day after the decision. We read each decision from the Fed's statement as soon as it is posted. The history comes from the Fed's published target range.
method_cpi: Past-year inflation compares the consumer price index with the same month a year earlier, before seasonal adjustment, which is how the Bureau of Labor Statistics headlines it. Past-month inflation uses the seasonally adjusted index. Core leaves out food and energy, whose prices jump around.
method_pce: The personal consumption expenditures price index from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, compared with the same month a year earlier and with the month before, both seasonally adjusted. Core leaves out food and energy. The Fed's 2% inflation goal is measured with this index.
method_jobs: Jobs added is the change in total nonfarm payrolls from the month before, seasonally adjusted. Each report also revises the two months before it, so earlier months show their latest revised numbers. The unemployment rate is the share of people looking for work who don't have a job.
method_gdp: Real GDP growth for the quarter, adjusted for inflation and expressed as an annual rate, as the Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes it. Each quarter is estimated three times, and later estimates replace earlier ones here.
method_claims: Initial claims for unemployment insurance filed in the week, seasonally adjusted, from the Department of Labor. The 4-week average smooths out one-off swings such as holidays.
